status: scenario-planning assumptions, not AGI timeline predictions

theses.title: Cognitive abundance
theses.thesis: The marginal cost of many forms of drafting, coding, explanation, search, translation, analysis and expert assistance is falling sharply.
theses.implication: Education cannot justify itself primarily by training students to produce routine cognitive outputs.

theses.title: Agentification
theses.thesis: AI is moving from answer generation toward systems that plan, use tools, maintain context and take actions with less human intervention.
theses.implication: Specification, permissions, monitoring, evaluator integrity, incident response and institutional accountability become general literacies.

theses.title: Evaluation becomes a bottleneck
theses.thesis: Capability benchmarks saturate quickly, real-world performance remains jagged, and increasingly autonomous systems create an evaluation gap.
theses.implication: Train verification, benchmark design, adversarial testing, calibration and the ability to know what cannot be reliably checked.

theses.title: Scientific acceleration with empirical bottlenecks
theses.thesis: AI increasingly contributes to scientific reasoning, biological modeling, literature synthesis and experimental design, but important claims still require real-world validation.
theses.implication: Teach science as model-plus-experiment, not model output; preserve laboratory and measurement competence.

theses.title: Work recomposition and shortened skill half-lives
theses.thesis: A large share of occupations is exposed to transformation, though exposure does not imply simple job elimination and effects remain heterogeneous.
theses.implication: Prioritize transferable foundations, learning autonomy, craft depth, enterprise and identity beyond a single occupational role.

theses.title: Epistemic hyperabundance
theses.thesis: Synthetic text, images, video and personalized persuasion drastically expand the volume of plausible information competing for finite attention.
theses.implication: Source ecology, primary evidence, attention, curation, provenance, rhetoric and epistemic institutions become more important.

theses.title: Personal AI mediation
theses.thesis: AI increasingly mediates learning, work, health information, decision support and emotionally meaningful interactions.
theses.implication: Teach reliance calibration and deliberately protect human relationships, mentorship, privacy, developmental autonomy and non-mediated experience.

theses.title: Power, compute and sovereignty
theses.thesis: Frontier capability depends on concentrated compute, chips, data centers, energy, capital and organizational capacity, making AI infrastructure a geopolitical and institutional question.
theses.implication: Human Worlds and Technical Systems must connect AI to energy, supply chains, state capacity, competition, standards and rights.

theses.title: Physical reality remains a bottleneck
theses.thesis: Digital and simulated competence is advancing faster than robust physical-world autonomy in uncontrolled environments.
theses.implication: Do not let a digital curriculum erase making, maintenance, logistics, fieldwork, embodiment or tacit physical knowledge.

theses.title: Institutional adaptation lags capability
theses.thesis: Education, evaluation, regulation and responsible-AI practice are adapting more slowly than capability and adoption.
theses.implication: Teach graduates to design and reform institutions, not merely operate within current ones.

theses.title: Meaning cannot be outsourced by productivity growth
theses.thesis: If machines become superior at economically valuable cognition, employment can no longer carry the full burden of identity, worth, education and purpose.
theses.implication: Education must explicitly include meaning, culture, relationships, civic membership, care, craft and self-authored commitments.

theses.title: Planetary and material constraints remain real
theses.thesis: AI itself consumes energy and depends on physical supply chains; abundant cognition does not abolish energy, material, ecological or infrastructure constraints.
theses.implication: Earth systems, energy, materials, ecology, infrastructure and long-horizon stewardship remain foundational.

theses.title: Plural values survive intelligence amplification
theses.thesis: More capable reasoning does not imply one uncontested answer to how people should live, distribute power, structure families, govern communities or use technology.
theses.implication: Teach philosophical disagreement, political legitimacy, cultural plurality, public reason and constitutional constraints.

theses.title: Human formation becomes more—not less—important
theses.thesis: As machines supply more cognition on demand, the risk grows that humans can obtain high-quality outputs without acquiring the knowledge, judgment or character that would make those outputs theirs in any meaningful sense.
theses.implication: Separate output quality from learning; require unaided floors, delayed transfer, making, dialogue, responsibility and ownership.
